mission: Test the Bigeh/Biggeh Abaton left-leg tradition against present archaeological topography, active fieldwork and submerged-site evidence without promoting a textual or ritual relic into a biological body-part claim.

textual_gate.source: Charly De Mare, Ci-git Osiris. L'Abaton de Biggeh d'apres les sources textuelles et iconographiques, BABELAO 5 (2016), pp. 1-46
textual_gate.finding: The Biggeh Abaton tradition explicitly locates the left leg of Osiris there and connects the sacred tomb, grove, Nile inundation and local topography.

topographic_gate.scholarly_candidate: Following Junker's reconstruction as reviewed by De Mare, the tomb and sacred grove are plausibly placed at the extreme south of the eastern coastal indentation of Biggeh.

candidate_coordinates.source_precision: plausible scholarly reconstruction, not excavated tomb coordinate

topographic_gate.required_control: Coordinate is a hypothesis for field comparison, not a discovered relic location.

modern_site_state.mission: Archaeological Mission on Biggeh Island, CNRS-SCA/CSA, directed by Gihane Zaki
modern_site_state.2026_public_status: Mission remains an active survey/state-of-site project; Louvre hosted Biggeh: Renaissance d'un tresor oublie on 11 June 2026.
water_damage: temple access stairs are regularly flooded
blocks from collapsed architectural elements lie in the immediate area and some underwater
internal/side sectors are heavily affected by fluctuating Nile/reservoir water and silt
modern_site_state.survey: 2024 mission used modern topographic mapping and systematic zoning/photographic comparison with historic documentation.
modern_site_state.planned_priority: Precise architectural survey and systematic excavation of the internal area between the pronaos and rocky mountain have been publicly described as key next programs.

next_gates: Overlay the De Mare/Junker candidate coordinate on the mission's current topographic zoning.
Determine whether the southern eastern-cove candidate contains a mound, cavity, subterranean feature, paleochannel, shrine, closed deposit or ancient sacred-grove soil horizon.
Determine whether the submerged quay/side rooms have bathymetry, sonar, underwater photogrammetry or diver inspection.
Check for geophysics such as GPR, electrical resistivity or other cavity detection where bedrock and access permit.
Recover object-level passports for any Osirian containers, djed objects, wrapped deposits, organic packages or cult equipment from Biggeh.
If material contents are found, classify plant/resin/animal/human/mineral/modern before any identity claim.
canonical_formula: LEFT_LEG_TEXT -> ABATON_TOPOGRAPHY -> ACTIVE_FIELD_ZONE -> SUBSURFACE/UNDERWATER_SURVEY -> CONTAINER/DEPOSIT -> MATERIAL -> PROVENANCE -> ONLY_THEN_IDENTITY
canonical_seal: BIGGEH GIVES US A TESTABLE LEFT-LEG SHRINE LOCATION, NOT A FOUND LEG.
